method.boundaryRule: Use rounded, contiguous elevation regimes supported by the candidate DEM distribution and official hiking-route examples. Exclude elevation tails dominated by unrelated lowland, glacier, climbing or non-representative summit terrain where appropriate.
method.weightRule: Staging priors rounded to 0.05 from the documented mix of lower, middle and upper hiking opportunities. These are route-catalogue proxies, not visitor-frequency estimates.
method.requiredFollowUp: Validate each prior against trail-network elevation coverage, Copernicus water/quality layers and ERA5-Land sampling. Keep destinationGeometryAndElevation.approved false until that evidence and manual representative-route QA are complete.

decisions.stagingHoldReason: The municipality polygon is dominated by high terrain and has no ERA5-Land model-orography candidate within the approved 600 m gate for the 1500-2200 m valley band. The gate must not be relaxed because snow, precipitation, humidity and wind are not elevation-corrected.
requiredBeforeReentry: Replace the municipality-wide valley representation with a reviewed trail-network or valley-corridor geometry.
Repeat the official ERA5-Land invariant-orography preflight and retain at least one valley candidate within 600 m.
Exclude glacier cells and repeat persistent-snow route QA for every retained band.
decisions.intendedHikingScope: Marked valley, mountain and alpine hiking routes in the municipality of Zermatt, ending below mountaineering-only terrain.

evidence.title: Zermatt Tourism hiking catalogue
evidence.observation: The official catalogue spans easy village routes through alpine hiking trails.

evidence.title: Matterhorn Glacier Trail
evidence.observation: A marked T3 hiking route covers 2,570–2,928 m; the Hörnli hiking route ends at 3,260 m before the climbing route begins.

decisions.intendedHikingScope: Valley, forest, panoramic and high-altitude hiking routes within the Grindelwald municipality, excluding glacier and climbing terrain.

evidence.title: Jungfrau Region hiking catalogue
evidence.observation: Official examples include the Eiger Trail at 1,616–2,348 m and Schynige Platte–First at 1,967–2,681 m.

decisions.stagingHoldReason: No Foothill sampling point satisfies both terrain and ERA5-Land model-orography representativeness. The locally suitable 47.3 N, 11.5 E point differs from the 639.3 m target by 767.4 m in the ERA5-Land model, while the remaining model-eligible candidate exceeds the 800 m Copernicus DEM terrain-mismatch gate.
requiredBeforeReentry: Replace the municipality-wide Foothill representation with reviewed lower-trail and mountain-access corridor geometry.
Repeat joint Copernicus DEM and ERA5-Land invariant-orography sampling and retain at least one Foothill point inside both gates.
Reconfirm whether lower urban walks belong in the hiking-climate product or require a separate city/foothill destination scope.

evidence.title: Zirbenweg trail

evidence.title: Ordino Estripagecs challenge
evidence.observation: The official peak challenge includes six peaks above 2,700 m and Serrera at 2,913 m.
